propositions: Test workers race on a shared git index: alpha's commit sweeps up beta's staged file, causing beta's subsequent commit to fail with rc=1 and empty stderr (nothing to commit).
The per-store advisory lock wraps each run_git_write call individually, but add and commit are two separate calls, leaving the pair unserialized and vulnerable to interleaving.
Worker assertions report only stderr, discarding stdout (which contains the diagnostic 'nothing to commit') and the command identity, making failures non-self-diagnosing.
Each worker must commit its own pathspec instead of the whole index so that losing the add/commit interleaving does not result in nothing staged.
Both concurrent writers must exit 0 and both commits must appear in git log; this requirement is preserved by the fix while eliminating the false negative.
